title: Front office PC can't get online
scenario: Ticket #4471 — Dana at the front desk reports that her PC (FRONT-OFFICE-03) can open the shared drive but no websites will load. Nobody else in the office has the problem. A contractor worked on her PC last week. Site standard: every workstation gets its address automatically from the office DHCP server.
tasks: Find out how the PC's network adapter is currently configured.
Test what the PC can and cannot reach.
Correct the configuration so it follows the site standard.
Prove the fix worked before you close the ticket.
hints: Start by looking, not changing. Which command shows the adapter's IP address, subnet mask and default gateway?
Try pinging something inside the office (the file server is 192.168.10.20) and something outside it (8.8.8.8). Compare the results.
Local traffic works and outside traffic fails. Which single setting tells the PC where to send traffic that is leaving the local network?
Compare the default gateway to the PC's own IP address and subnet mask. Is the gateway on the same network as the PC?
The site standard is DHCP. Open Network Settings and set the adapter to obtain its address automatically, then test again.

checks.label: Checked the adapter configuration before changing anything
checks.pass: You ran ipconfig before touching any settings, so you knew the starting point.
checks.fail: You changed settings without first running ipconfig. Gather information before you change anything, or you cannot tell what the original fault was.

checks.label: Tested connectivity before changing anything
checks.pass: You used ping to see what was reachable before making a change.
checks.fail: You did not test connectivity with ping before making a change. Testing local and outside addresses is what narrows this fault down to the gateway.
checks.practice: Tested the symptom before making changes

checks.label: The PC can reach the internet
checks.pass: The PC can now reach outside addresses and resolve names.
checks.fail: The PC still cannot reach the internet. Its default gateway must be an address on its own network (192.168.10.x); it was set to 192.168.1.1.
checks.practice: The PC can reach the internet

checks.label: The adapter follows the site standard (DHCP)
checks.pass: The adapter obtains its address automatically, as the site standard requires.
checks.fail: The adapter is still set to a manual (static) address. Even with a corrected gateway, the ticket said every workstation must use DHCP.
checks.practice: The fix follows the site standard

checks.label: Verified the fix with a successful test to an outside address
checks.pass: After your last change you confirmed an outside address replies.
checks.fail: You did not run a successful ping to an outside address after your last change. A fix is not finished until you have verified it.
checks.practice: Verified the fix after the last change
